newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian court jails ex-secret police officials.
newsitem.headline: Albanian court jails ex-secret police officials.

text.p: An Albanian court has jailed two former senior police officials for deleting files of the former communist secret police, daily Rilindja Demokratike said on Wednesday.
The paper said a Tirana court sentenced Irakli Kocollari, head of the notorious Sigurimi police, to six years in jail and Vladimir Hysi, former interior minister, to 18 months for abuse of power.
"The court thinks the defendants have committed the penal act of abuse of power...and for that they should be sentenced," Tirana court judge Shaqir Hasani was quoted as saying.
Kocollari and Hysi "destroyed documents of special importance...which demonstrated the physical and psychological terror exercised by Sigurimi at the time", he added.
The much-feared Sigurimi was dismantled in 1991 after the collapse of communism in Albania and reorganised as the National Information Service (SHIK).
Hysi and Kocollari headed the public order ministry and the secret police National Information Service respectively during 1991 and 1992, following Albania's first multi-party elections.

The reformed communist party won the elections, changing its name to the Socialist Party before losing the second general election in March 1992 to the conservative Democratic Party led by President Sali Berisha.
